content.user_title: Apply Analogical Reasoning to New Problems
content.value_statement: Teams often face new markets or products without a direct playbook. This skill maps proven source cases to a new target and adapts the plan.
actual_capabilities: Selects relevant source cases using similarity, outcome quality, recency, success, and context overlap.
Maps source objects, relations, constraints, mechanisms, and success factors to a target context.
Separates preserved, modified, and broken relationships before proposing adaptations.
Produces an adapted plan with phases, milestones, timeline, confidence, and uncertainty.
Flags mapping quality issues such as surface similarity, over-transfer, and under-adaptation.
Suggests next reasoning modes when causal testing or assumption validation is needed.
limitations: Requires source cases with enough detail about outcomes, constraints, and mechanisms.
Cannot prove a transferred pattern will work in the new context.
May miss hidden differences if the user provides shallow context.
Does not replace market research, user interviews, or causal validation.

use_cases.title: Plan a Market Expansion
use_cases.description: Map a successful launch in one vertical to a new vertical, then adapt sales, onboarding, and success metrics.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Product Playbook
use_cases.description: Transfer lessons from an existing product workflow to a new product line while marking what must change.

use_cases.title: Compare Strategic Options
use_cases.description: Evaluate multiple past cases and choose the source analogy with the strongest structural fit.

prompt_templates.title: Map One Known Case
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single source analogy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use analogical reasoning. Source case: [known case]. Target situation: [new situation]. Map the key objects, relations, constraints, and likely adaptations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Best Source
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt when several prior examples may apply.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these source cases for my target: [cases]. Score structural similarity, outcome quality, recency, success, and context overlap. Select the best source.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Adapted Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for translating a source pattern into execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map [source case] to [target context]. List preserved, modified, and broken relationships. Produce a phased plan with milestones, timeline, confidence, and uncertainties.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test the Analogy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for reviewing transfer risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this analogy: [mapping]. Find surface similarities, over-transfer, under-adaptation, and missing context differences. Recommend changes before execution.

output_examples.input: A team wants to adapt a successful DTC launch playbook to a B2B marketplace launch.
output: Selected source: DTC platform launch with strong integration similarity.
Preserved: marketplace discovery, integration-first positioning, and fast value demonstration.
Modified: self-serve onboarding becomes assisted onboarding because B2B buying is slower.
Plan: partnership setup, pilot customers, case studies, then referral-led expansion.

output_examples.input: A product manager wants to transfer a fashion sizing workflow to home goods recommendations.
output: Mapped objects: fashion brand becomes home goods brand, fit concern becomes space compatibility.
Broken relation: body measurements do not transfer directly to room dimensions.
New capability: room measurement capture and dimension-based recommendation logic.
Confidence: moderate, with technical uncertainty around visualization complexity.

output_examples.input: An operations team has three prior rollout examples and needs the best analogy.
output: Best source: the rollout with the closest workflow dependencies and documented metrics.
Rejected source: high revenue outcome but weak structural similarity.
Next step: validate the two largest context differences before copying the playbook.

best_practices: Provide source cases with documented outcomes, metrics, constraints, and timeframes.
Focus mapping on relationships and mechanisms, not surface labels.
Use the uncertainty section to plan validation before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a source playbook without listing context differences.
Do not rely on a single weak analogy when better source cases exist.
Do not treat analogy as proof of future success.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It transfers lessons from known source cases to new situations using explicit structural mapping and adaptation.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a new problem resembles a past market, product, rollout, or operating model.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Provide the target situation, candidate source cases, outcomes, constraints, and known differences.

faq.question: Can it choose between multiple analogies?
faq.answer: Yes. It scores candidate sources by structural similarity, documented outcome, recency, success, and context overlap.

faq.question: Does it validate the plan?
faq.answer: It identifies uncertainty and quality risks, but users should validate assumptions with evidence.

faq.question: Does it require external tools?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a reasoning framework and does not require command execution, network access, or scripts.
